questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question_text: The number of alkali metal(s), from $Li,K,Cs$ , Rb having ionization enthalpy greater than $400kJ$ $mol^{-1}$ and forming stable super oxide is _____________.
questions.question_html: The number of alkali metal(s), from $Li,K,Cs$ , Rb having ionization enthalpy greater than $400kJ$ $mol^{-1}$ and forming stable super oxide is _____________.
questions.explanation_text:
Li does not form superoxide. K, Rb and Cs form stable super oxides but Cs has
ionisation enthalpy less than 400 kJ. While K and Rb
have ionisation enthalpy greater than 400 kJ mol –1 .
questions.explanation_html:
Li does not form superoxide.

K, Rb and Cs form stable super oxides but Cs has ionisation enthalpy less than 400 kJ. While K and Rb have ionisation enthalpy greater than 400 kJ mol–1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question_text: BeO reacts with HF in presence of ammonia to give [A] which on thermal decomposition produces [B] and ammonium fluoride. Oxidation state of Be in [A] is ____________.
questions.question_html: BeO reacts with HF in presence of ammonia to give [A] which on thermal decomposition produces [B] and ammonium fluoride. Oxidation state of Be in [A] is ____________.
questions.explanation_text: $BeO+2NH_{3}+4HF \longrightarrow \underset{\text{(A)}}{(NH_{4})_{2}[BeF_{4}]}$ $(NH_{4})_{2}(BeF_{4})\overset{\text{Heating}}{\longrightarrow}\underset{\text{(B)}}{BeF_{2}}+2NH_{4}F$ Oxidation State of Be in $(A)$ is $(+2)$
questions.explanation_html:
$BeO+2NH_{3}+4HF \longrightarrow \underset{\text{(A)}}{(NH_{4})_{2}[BeF_{4}]}$

$(NH_{4})_{2}(BeF_{4})\overset{\text{Heating}}{\longrightarrow}\underset{\text{(B)}}{BeF_{2}}+2NH_{4}F$

Oxidation State of Be in $(A)$ is $(+2)$
